newsitem.title: USA: ASARCO stake in Grupo Mexico still proves thorny.
newsitem.headline: ASARCO stake in Grupo Mexico still proves thorny.

text.p: ASARCO said it was still no nearer to pulling the plug on its 23.6 percent stake in Grupo Mexico, the mining company located south of the U.S. border.

ASARCO's chairman, president and chief executive officer Richard de J Osborne admitted to analysts on Friday there was no quick solution to selling the stake, and no negotiations were being held with GMexico, contrary to some reports.
"There are no such negotiations now underway," Osborne said.
The stake in GMexico was worth in excess of $300 million, he added.

The issue has become a bone of contention between the two companies who don't see eye to eye on how the shares should be sold. ASARCO was unhappy with the return on its investment in GMexico, analysts have said.
"We and they have our own valuation models. We have not found a common meeting ground," Osborne said, adding he was not optimistic about any agreement with GMexico in the near term.
"We do plan to sell that interest when market conditions permit doing so," he reiterated.
After copper prices tumbled in the wake of the Sumitomo scandal last year, Osborne said it has not been a good time to sell the GMexico stake.
GMexico is top heavy in copper exposure with about 68 percent of revenues from red metal sales.
Neverthless ASARCO was looking at alternatives to selling the stocks such as offering shares in ASARCO in exchange for GMexico shares.

However, this would present considerable hurdles and may not be practical because GMexico shares would need to be registered in the U.S. where trading faced more stringent Securities and Exchanges Commission regulations, Osborne said.
